question: The directive principles of state policy in Indian’s constitution are borrowed from the constitution of ____. (RRB ALP Fitter (23/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: Germany
Canada
Ireland
Britain
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ireland

Explanation:
The directive principles of state policy (DPSP) in the Indian Constitution are borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland. These principles guide the government in policy-making but are not judicially enforceable. DPSP aims to establish social and economic democracy. They are enshrined in Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Indian Constitution. Inspired by Ireland, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar described them as the 'conscience of the Constitution'. The main objective of DPSP is to establish a welfare state. These principles help the government achieve goals like social justice, economic equality, and freedom from exploitation.

☛ Part IV of Indian Constitution → Articles 36-51
☛ Nature of DPSP → Non-justiciable but guiding
☛ Main objective of DPSP → Welfare state
☛ Inspiration for DPSP → Constitution of Ireland

question: When did the Constituent Assembly of India meet for the first time? (RRB ALP (Electrician) (22/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: 9th December 1946
19th December 1946
26th November 1956
26th December 1946
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 9th December 1946

Explanation:
The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly of India was held on 9th December 1946 in New Delhi. It was chaired by Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha, the interim president of the assembly. Later, Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as the permanent president. The Constituent Assembly was formed under the Cabinet Mission Plan. It had a total of 389 members, of which 296 were elected from provincial assemblies and 93 represented princely states. The Muslim League boycotted the first meeting. The assembly adopted the Constitution on 26th November 1949 and it came into effect on 26th January 1950.

☛ Permanent President of Constituent Assembly → Rajendra Prasad
☛ Plan under which Constituent Assembly was formed → Cabinet Mission Plan

☛ Date of adoption of Constitution → 26th November 1949

question: Funds belonging to the Government of India are kept in- (RRB JE ME (31/08/2019) CBT 2)
options: Public Account of India
Consolidated fund of India
All of the options
Contingency Fund of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is All of the options

Explanation:
Funds belonging to the Government of India are kept in three main accounts: the Consolidated Fund of India, the Contingency Fund of India, and the Public Account of India. The Consolidated Fund receives all tax revenues, non-tax revenues, and loan receipts. The Contingency Fund is used for emergency expenditures, while the Public Account handles transactions like savings banks, provident funds, etc., that are not part of the government's own account. Together, they manage all government funds.

question: Which of the following Articles deals with 'Prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour'? (RRB JE CBT-I (22/05/2019) Shift 2)
options: Article 29
Article 27
Article 30
Article 23
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 23

Explanation:
Article 23 of the Indian Constitution prohibits traffic in human beings and forced labour. It is a fundamental right under the Right against Exploitation. This article bans begar (forced labour without payment) and other similar forms of exploitation. Any violation of this provision is punishable by law. The only exception is compulsory service for public purposes imposed by the state, provided it does not discriminate on grounds of religion, race, caste, class or sex. Article 23 protects all persons, not just citizens, from human trafficking and bonded labour. In contrast, Article 27 deals with exemption from taxes for religious promotion, Article 29 protects the cultural and educational rights of minorities, and Article 30 gives minorities the right to establish educational institutions.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ What is the exception to forced labour? → Compulsory service for public purposes imposed by the state
☛ Article 23 is part of which Part of the Constitution? → Part III (Fundamental Rights)
☛ Article 23 is a right against what? → Exploitation
☛ Who is protected under Article 23? → All persons (not just citizens)

question: What should be the minimum age to get the Rajya Sabha membership? (RRB JE CBT-I (22/05/2019) Shift 2)
options: 25 years
35 years
18 years
30 years
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 30 years

Explanation:
According to Article 84 of the Indian Constitution, the minimum age to become a member of the Rajya Sabha is 30 years, while for the Lok Sabha it is 25 years. The Rajya Sabha being the upper house requires more experience and maturity, hence a higher age limit. Other conditions for Rajya Sabha membership include being a citizen of India and not holding any office of profit. The term of Rajya Sabha members is 6 years, with one-third of members retiring every two years. This age requirement ensures that members have sufficient life experience to contribute meaningfully to legislative debates and decision-making.

question: Which of the following created the office of Governor General of India? (RRB JE (23/05/2019) Shift 1 CBT 1)

solution:

Explanation:
The Charter Act of 1833 created the office of the Governor General of India. This act made the Governor General of Bengal the Governor General of India and granted him administrative authority over all British Indian provinces. Prior to this, the Governor General was only the head of the Bengal Presidency. The act also conferred legislative powers on the Governor General, allowing him to make laws. This laid the foundation for centralized administration in India. The Governor General also gained control over financial matters. This act was a significant step towards the unification of British rule in India.

question: Which of the following Articles in the Constitution grants us the Right to Equality? (RRB JE (25/05/2019) Shift 2 CBT 1)

question: Which Article of Indian Constitution gives the procedure for impeachment of the President? (RRB JE (25/05/2019) Shift 3 CBT 1)
options: Article 61
Article 48
Article 42
Article 59
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 61

Explanation:
Article 61 of the Indian Constitution deals with the procedure for impeachment of the President. It states that the President can be impeached for violation of the Constitution. The impeachment process can be initiated in either House of Parliament. The charge must be signed by at least one-fourth of the total members of that House, and a 14-day notice must be given. The resolution must be passed by a two-thirds majority of the total membership of that House. Then the other House investigates the charge, and if it also passes the resolution by a two-thirds majority, the President is removed. Article 48 relates to agriculture and animal husbandry, Article 42 to work and maternity leave, and Article 59 to qualifications of the President.

☛ Ground for impeachment of President → Violation of Constitution

Solution: सही उत्तर है सच्चिदानंद सिन्हा

Explanation:
भारत की संविधान सभा की पहली बैठक 9 दिसंबर 1946 को हुई थी। इस बैठक की अध्यक्षता सच्चिदानंद सिन्हा ने की, जो उस समय सबसे वरिष्ठ सदस्य थे। बाद में 11 दिसंबर 1946 को डॉ. राजेन्द्र प्रसाद को स्थायी अध्यक्ष चुना गया। डॉ. बी.आर. अम्बेडकर मसौदा समिति के अध्यक्ष थे, जबकि पी. उपेन्द्र एक अन्य सदस्य थे। इस प्रकार, उद्घाटन बैठक की अध्यक्षता सच्चिदानंद सिन्हा ने की।
